To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the optimal management strategy for a forest is a combination of clear-cutting and continuous cover forestry.
the economic optimum of a forest management problem is either a clear-cut with a given rotation length or continuous harvesting with a given harvest rate.

(i) continuous cover forestry and clear-cuts can both be locally optimal forest management strategies, (ii) the relative value of large diameter trees determines whether clear-cuts or continuous cover forestry is locally optimal, and (iii) the relative value is a decreasing function of discounting.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the economics of forest harvesting and management in the context of naturally regenerating, mixed-species, heterogeneous forests.
the economic implications of the natural regeneration of forest ecosystems.
an economic model for the management of heterogeneous, naturally regenerating forest stands.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
clear-cuts and/or continuous cover forestry may be optimal depending on the initial stand and the discount rate.
continuous cover forestry is the preferred solution for most situations.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the economics of naturally regenerating, mixed-species forests are complex and that clear-cuts and/or continuous harvesting are not necessarily optimal.
continuous cover forestry is a locally optimal management strategy for heterogeneous, natural forests.
, under a wide variety of conditions, continuous harvesting is the optimal solution for naturally regenerating forests.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a forest management model that includes nonconvexity can yield both clear-cutting and continuous cover forestry.

the economic model for naturally regenerated forests is not a standard optimal control problem, but rather is a more general class of problems, and that the standard approach of using the maximum principle to solve the problem may lead to suboptimal solutions.
a model of naturally regenerating forests can yield both clear-cut and continuous cover solutions.
